newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel plans measures to enhance competition.
newsitem.headline: Israel plans measures to enhance competition.

text.p: Israel will open intercity bus lines to competition and license a third cellular telephone operator as part of a move to widen competition in the economy, according to a Treasury white paper released on Tuesday.
The wide-ranging programme, which also plans liberalisation measures in energy, agriculture and the labour market, will go to the cabinet for approval on Wednesday.

Treasury officials said Finance Minister Dan Meridor would meet with Histadrut labour federation chief Amir Peretz this evening to discuss the changes, some of which are likely to be opposed by unions.
Increased competition is aimed at lowering prices for consumers, the paper said. Other measures are aimed at making the public sector more efficient.

According to the paper, a special interministerial committee will be formed by January 15 to present recommendations on public transport deregulation. By July 31, the government will publish tenders for companies to compete with the Egged and Dan bus cooperatives on three intercity bus lines.

A tender for a third cellphone operator to compete with Pelephone and Cellcom will be published no later than July 1, 1997. Pelephone is a joint venture between the main telephone company, Bezeq Israel Telecom, and Motorola Israel.
The Treasury said it also planned to amend the Bezeq Law to enable people to receive direct satellite television broadcasts.
In the energy sector, the Treasury said it planned regulatory changes that would lead to the building of more petrol stations and other measures.
The paper also calls for ending state-owned Agrexco's monopoly on agricultural exports. Israel's citrus sector was demonopolised five years ago.

The Treasury also said it wants to step up tenders of state-owned land to increase the amount of land tendered for future building to the equivalent to 400,000 housing units by 1999. Tenders for 1997 and 1998 will be for land zoned for 50,000 units.

Among other measures, a committee will be formed to recommend whether the legal retirement age should be raised from age 65 for men and age 60 for women and the port tax adjusted. For importers it will be lower to 1 percent from 1.3 percent while for exporters it will be raised to 0.5 percent from 0.2 percent
